key_insight: Neutral ethylenediamine removes excess surface tin and restores tin–lead stoichiometry, improving electron extraction and reducing interfacial recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface defects offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free tin–lead perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide passivation.
Use atomistic simulations to examine vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation.
Link surface reconstruction to electronic character, C60 electron extraction, and device performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term operational stability or manufacturing-scale reproducibility of the surface treatment.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
